newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian 88 climbs on natgas well results.
newsitem.headline: Canadian 88 climbs on natgas well results.

text.p: Shares of Canadian 88 Energy Corp jumped in brisk volume on Wednesday as results from a much-watched natural gas well in Alberta suggested the firm may have discovered the company-maker it was hoping for.

Canadian 88, which on Monday said it believed its deep and expensive Waterton wildcat well in the Alberta foothills encountered "significant" reserves, climbed C$0.33 to C$5.30 on turnover of 3.4 million shares.
The stock, which was the Toronto Stock Exchange's most-active issue on Wednesday, jumped to a new intra-day high earlier in the session.

The company said on Monday the C$4-million well, drilled on Shell Canada Ltd land in southwest Alberta, hit its total depth of 4,146 metres and casing was being run to the base of the Mississippian geological formation.
The Waterton well was expected to be on stream in the next 90 to 120 days, it said.
But before the well starts flowing, the company plans to drill deeper into the Devonian formation to gauge the presence of gas.
Analysts said on Wednesday that Canadian 88 may have encountered more than the 300 billion cubic feet it had hoped to hit with the Waterton prospect.
Company president Greg Noval said earlier this year that if the well lived up to its advance billing, Canadian 88 reserves would double from the then-300 BCF mark.
"This is a tremendous, tremendous asset play," said ScotiaMcleod analyst Rob Robinson, who rates Canadian 88 as a strong buy, despite the tripling of its stock price in the last year.
Reserves from the well could top 500 BCF if the company hits gas in the lower zone, Robinson said.
He said production from the field could hit 100 million cubic feet per day by the end of 1997, if the company plans to drill four more Waterton wells go ahead as expected.
Robinson said he expected Canadian 88's production to leap to 240 million cubic feet per day with the Waterton play and the company's Olds-Crossfield gas play, also in Alberta.
Canadian 88 produced about 50 MMCFD in the second quarter of this year. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
